data.hypothesis: With the existing two-target-per-thread kernel, reducing the block from 128 to 32 threads while matching the tile to 64 outputs reduces nominal per-CTA register demand, potentially changing residency; the increased number of CTAs may offset that. The effect is hardware-dependent, so no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: These results apply to the measured factor-two configurations in this campaign; they do not establish behavior on other hardware.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 64- and 128-thread factor-two configurations were nearly identical at about 0.002617 seconds and slower than the 0.001847-second baseline; the 256-thread factor-two configuration was slower still at about 0.002727 seconds. These timings do not identify register use or occupancy as the cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 32-thread configuration with the official correctness and timing checks; use compiler/device resource reports if available before attributing any outcome to occupancy.

data.notes: This changes only launch settings. The existing kernel retains independent bounds checks for both targets, covering arbitrary N and partial tiles, and uses no shared-memory staging. Register and occupancy measurements were not provided; the controller must run the full correctness suite and official timing metric.
transformations: Set the block size to 32 threads and items_per_block to 64, preserving the existing factor-two target mapping.
Keep shared_memory_bytes at zero; retain the kernel's per-target bounds checks and separate accumulators.
